verifications.claim: Artemis II mission launched on April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'blasted off from Florida on Wednesday evening... at 6:35 p.m. Eastern time' (article dated 2026/04/01); R3: 'Launch date April 1, 2026, 22:35:12 UTC (6:35:12 p.m. EDT)'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the exact launch date and time.

verifications.claim: Artemis II mission features a four-person crew—Reid Wiseman (Commander), Victor Glover (Pilot), Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen (Mission Specialists).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Mr. Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen'; R3: 'commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, and mission specialist Christina Koch... mission specialist Jeremy Hansen'; R6: 'Commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, and mission specialist Christina Koch... mission specialist Jeremy Hansen'
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm the exact crew composition and roles.

verifications.claim: Artemis II crew is on a 10-day journey around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '10-day mission'; R2: 'lasting less than 10 days'; R3: '9 days, 1 hour, 32 minutes'; R6: 'approximately 10-day mission'
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently describe it as a ~10-day lunar flyby mission.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed flight test of the SLS rocket.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'the second flight of the Space Launch System (SLS) and the first crewed flight'; R6: 'NASA’s first mission with crew aboard our foundational deep space rocket, the SLS'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state it is the first crewed SLS flight (after uncrewed Artemis I).

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed flight test of the Orion spacecraft.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'the first crewed flight of the Orion spacecraft'
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated in R3.
